hooks.text: One cosmic object is distant enough to change our night sky forever.
A star nursery 160,000 light-years away could cast shadows on Earth.
160,000 light-years away, a cosmic factory shines bright enough to cast shadows.

title: The Star Factory That Casts Shadows
description: The Tarantula Nebula is so luminous that if it replaced the Orion Nebula, its light would cast visible shadows on Earth at night.

beats.text: One cosmic object is distant enough to change our night sky forever.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope image of the Tarantula Nebula showing glowing gas, 2022

beats.text: Our familiar Orion Nebula is close, but jump 160,000 light-years into deep space.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope mosaic of the Orion Nebula, 2006
queries: Hubble Space Telescope Orion Nebula mosaic 2006

beats.text: There, inside the Large Magellanic Cloud galaxy, lies the colossal Tarantula Nebula.
beats.visual: Wide-field view of the Large Magellanic Cloud showing 30 Doradus, 2010
queries: Large Magellanic Cloud wide field photograph ESO

beats.text: Spanning roughly 1,000 light-years across, it is the most energetic star factory in our Local Group.
beats.visual: VLT Survey Telescope panoramic view of the Tarantula Nebula, 2012
queries: VLT Survey Telescope Tarantula Nebula ESO 2012

beats.text: At its heart, cluster R136 contains some of the most massive stars ever discovered.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope photograph of the central star cluster R136, 2009
queries: Hubble R136 star cluster Tarantula Nebula

beats.text: This dense star cluster unleashes a torrent of radiation that powers the entire cloud.
beats.visual: Composite image of radiation and gas in R136 by Hubble and Chandra, 2011

beats.text: If moved to Orion's distance, this glowing giant would cover forty percent of the night sky.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of the Tarantula Nebula dominating the night sky above Earth, 2021
queries: Tarantula Nebula replacing Orion Nebula artist concept

beats.text: Its extreme luminosity would turn midnight into a world of visible shadows.
